question.text: Off-market transfers in the client's account are permitted for:

answer.text: Only for permitted cases such as settlement of clients' own trades, margin/collateral for clients' own positions, dealing in unlisted securities, specific client consent for each transaction, or any other SEBI-specified reason

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series XXI-A workbook (page 98), off-market transfers are limited to specific permitted cases: settlement of clients' own trades, margin or collateral for clients' own positions, dealing in unlisted securities, specific client consent for each transaction, or any other reason as may be specified by SEBI. The Trap: Random convenience, the portfolio manager's personal needs, or STT avoidance are not permitted grounds; the SEBI-specified residual exception is the only catch-all. Note: Source: NISM Series XXI-A workbook, page 98.
